title: DEC-301 item 1: Developer ID signing and notarization of the Ward release (draft the path first)
summary: Accepted by opum-doc as the build design (DEC-301 (a3)); the signing path reference is the deliverable, nothing is built.
description: DEC-301 item 1 (opum-doc DEC-301 (a2), 2026-11-26): the operator registered the Apple Developer account. Step 1 is a DRAFT of the signing and notarization path for opum-doc acceptance, docs only: no signing code, workflow edit, secret or install. Fixed by opum-doc: no session holds the key or notarization credential; signing runs in the release workflow on reviewed main with credentials in a protected GitHub environment unless the draft shows a reason not; the draft lists every operator step in order as one batch; the Homebrew tap and saws pin wait for a signed release (ADR 0029). Later workflow or release-path changes need their own dispatch-floor read and an Opus review.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A docs-only draft names the signing and notarization path, every operator step in order as one batch, and the open design choices, and is delivered to opum-doc for acceptance
No signing code, workflow change, secret or install is made before opum-doc accepts the draft

implementationNotes: review.toml: the new reference is declared (#recommended-path) in the review profile, which sat at its token budget, so ADR 0006 and 0007 are narrowed to #decision to stay within it. A narrowing, not a re-budget or an exemption.
Draft accepted by opum-doc as DEC-301 (a3); the decided choices are folded in. The release.yml build is a separate task.
